indicators.name: New orders, electrical equipment manufacturing (NAICS 3353)
indicators.link: US factory orders for transformers, switchgear, motors and generators; the industry aggregate behind Eaton, Hubbell, Powell and GE Vernova's electrification products.

indicators.name: Unfilled orders, electrical equipment manufacturing
indicators.link: Industry backlog of electrical equipment; rising unfilled orders signal lead times and pricing power.

indicators.name: Shipments, electrical equipment manufacturing
indicators.link: Industry revenue proxy for electrical equipment; coincident with company sales.

indicators.name: New orders, ventilation, heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment
indicators.link: Thermal-management demand (data center cooling for Vertiv and Modine) within a broader HVAC aggregate.

indicators.name: New orders, construction machinery manufacturing
indicators.link: US orders for excavators, loaders, dozers and the like; Caterpillar Construction Industries' home market.

indicators.name: Shipments, construction machinery manufacturing
indicators.link: Industry sales of construction machinery; coincident with Caterpillar's construction segment.

indicators.name: New orders, mining, oil and gas field machinery
indicators.link: Mining and oilfield equipment orders; Caterpillar Resource Industries and part of Energy & Transportation.

indicators.name: New orders, industrial machinery manufacturing (incl. semiconductor machinery)
indicators.link: NAICS 3332 includes semiconductor manufacturing machinery made in the US.

indicators.name: Unfilled orders, machinery
indicators.link: Aggregate machinery backlog including turbines and engines.

indicators.name: New orders, nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft
indicators.link: The standard business-investment orders gauge; broad demand backdrop for industrial equipment.

indicators.name: Total construction spending
indicators.unit: USD m, seasonally adjusted annual rate
indicators.link: Construction activity drives machine utilisation, fleet replacement and rental demand.

indicators.name: Nonresidential construction spending
indicators.link: Commercial, industrial and infrastructure building; electrical content per project is high.

indicators.name: Highway and street construction spending
indicators.link: Earthmoving and paving demand (Caterpillar construction equipment, United Rentals).

indicators.name: Private manufacturing construction spending
indicators.link: Factory construction (chip fabs, battery plants) needs electrical gear and site equipment.

indicators.name: Power construction spending
indicators.link: Generation, transmission and distribution construction; Quanta and MasTec's core market.

indicators.name: Housing starts
indicators.link: Residential construction demand for compact and general construction equipment.

indicators.name: PPI, electric power and specialty transformers
indicators.link: Output price of transformers; pricing power in grid equipment under tight supply.

indicators.name: PPI, switchgear and switchboard apparatus
indicators.link: Output price of switchgear (Eaton, Powell, Schneider, ABB).

indicators.name: PPI, turbine and turbine generator set units
indicators.link: Output price of turbines and generator sets (GE Vernova gas power, Caterpillar Solar Turbines).

indicators.name: PPI, construction machinery
indicators.link: Price realisation on construction equipment, a stated Caterpillar margin driver.

indicators.name: PPI, iron and steel
indicators.link: Main material input cost for machinery and electrical equipment.

indicators.name: Global price of copper
indicators.link: Input cost for windings, cables and busbars; also a mining-capex signal for Resource Industries.

indicators.name: Industrial production, mining
indicators.link: Mining activity drives haul-truck hours, parts and services and fleet replacement.

indicators.name: Industrial production, drilling oil and gas wells
indicators.link: Well-site engines, compression and gas turbines (Caterpillar Energy & Transportation, Cummins).

indicators.name: Industrial production, semiconductors and other electronic components
indicators.link: Chip output; utilisation drives tool demand with a lag.

indicators.name: Industrial production, agriculture, construction and mining machinery
indicators.link: US output of heavy machinery; production volume behind Caterpillar's US plants.

indicators.name: Industrial production, electrical equipment
indicators.link: Physical output of transformers, switchgear and motors in the US.

indicators.name: Freight transportation services index
indicators.link: For-hire freight volume (truck, rail, pipeline, water, air); a coincident gauge of goods activity.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capital expenditure (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META)
indicators.link: Cash spent on data centers and servers by the four largest cloud operators; the funding source of data center power and cooling orders.

indicators.name: Utility capital expenditure (22 US investor-owned utilities)
indicators.link: Transmission, distribution and generation investment; buys transformers, switchgear, poles, connectors and construction labour.

indicators.name: Private construction spending, data centers
indicators.link: Value of data center construction put in place; electrical and mechanical systems are a large share.

indicators.name: Electricity demand, Dominion zone (Northern Virginia data center cluster)
indicators.link: Load growth where the largest data center market draws power.

indicators.name: Electricity demand, ERCOT (Texas)
indicators.link: Texas load growth from data centers, industry and crypto mining.

indicators.name: Electricity demand, lower 48 states
indicators.link: National load; demand for generation and grid capacity.

indicators.name: Retail electricity sales, Virginia commercial sector
indicators.link: Data centers are billed as commercial load in Virginia; the cleanest public meter on data center power.

indicators.name: Retail electricity sales, Texas commercial sector
indicators.link: Commercial load in Texas, a fast-growing data center market.

indicators.name: Planned natural gas turbine capacity due within 24 months (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Combustion and combined-cycle turbines that developers report as planned; GE Vernova and Siemens Energy gas turbines, plus transformers and switchyards per plant.

indicators.name: Planned battery storage capacity due within 24 months (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Each battery project needs inverters, transformers and switchgear.

indicators.name: Planned solar capacity due within 24 months (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Utility-scale solar construction (Quanta, MasTec) and its collection-system electrical gear.

indicators.name: Planned wind capacity due within 24 months (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Onshore wind additions (GE Vernova wind segment, construction contractors).

indicators.name: Planned internal-combustion engine and fuel cell capacity due within 24 months (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Reciprocating engines and fuel cells (Caterpillar, Cummins, Bloom Energy) at grid-connected plants.

indicators.name: Natural gas turbine capacity entering operation (EIA-860M)
indicators.link: Turbines delivered and commissioned; equipment revenue is recognised before or around this date.

indicators.name: US imports of liquid dielectric transformers above 10 MVA (HS 850423)
indicators.link: Most large power transformers used in the US are imported; imports track utility and data center substation demand.

indicators.name: US imports of switchboards and control panels (HS 8537)
indicators.link: Imported switchgear competes with and supplements Eaton, Schneider and ABB US output.

indicators.name: US imports of electric generating sets (HS 8502)
indicators.link: Backup and prime power generator sets; data center backup power demand.

indicators.name: US imports of computers and servers (HS 8471)
indicators.link: Servers arriving for installation; IT load that must be powered and cooled.

indicators.name: US exports of earthmoving machinery (HS 8429)
indicators.link: Bulldozers, graders, loaders and excavators shipped abroad; Caterpillar is the largest US exporter.

indicators.name: US exports of semiconductor manufacturing machines (HS 8486)
indicators.link: Tools shipped from US plants of Applied Materials, Lam Research and KLA.

indicators.name: Japan exports of semiconductor manufacturing machines (HS 8486)
indicators.link: Tokyo Electron and peers' shipments; a read on global wafer-fab equipment spending.

indicators.name: Korea imports of semiconductor manufacturing machines (HS 8486)
indicators.link: Samsung and SK hynix tool purchases arriving in Korea.

indicators.name: Indeed job postings index, electrical engineering (US)
indicators.link: Employers add engineers ahead of capacity and project work.

indicators.name: Indeed job postings index, construction (US)
indicators.link: Hiring intentions of contractors ahead of project starts.

indicators.name: Indeed job postings index, installation and maintenance (US)
indicators.link: Electricians and technicians install and service electrical and cooling equipment.

indicators.name: Indeed job postings index, production and manufacturing (US)
indicators.link: Factory hiring as manufacturers raise output.

indicators.name: New natural gas generation interconnection requests (MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO)
indicators.link: Developers file for grid access years before ordering turbines; a long-lead signal for gas power.

indicators.name: New battery storage interconnection requests (MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO)
indicators.link: Storage requests become inverter, transformer and switchgear orders if built.

indicators.name: All new generation interconnection requests (MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO)
indicators.link: Total developer demand for grid connections; most requests are later withdrawn.

indicators.name: Texas data center construction registrations, estimated cost (TDLR TABS)
indicators.link: Texas law requires registering commercial building projects above $50,000 with an accessibility review before construction; data center registrations are a public, dated pipeline of new builds.

indicators.name: EU contract awards for transformers, switchgear and power cables (TED)
indicators.link: European utilities' published equipment awards; demand for ABB, Siemens Energy, Schneider, Hitachi.

sources.name: SEC EDGAR (XBRL company facts, filing index, filings)
sources.terms: Public data; SEC fair-access policy (declared User-Agent, at most 10 requests per second)
sources.vintage: filing - every value carries the acceptance time of the filing that first reported it; restatements are new vintages
sources.content: Quarterly revenue, costs, operating income and remaining performance obligations for 17 companies; segment revenue from 879 XBRL instance documents; capital expenditure of 4 hyperscalers and 22 utilities; 8-K release times and press releases; annual-report text for the mapping

sources.name: ALFRED / FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (Census M3 survey, construction spending, PPI, industrial production, copper, freight)
sources.terms: FRED terms of use; underlying series are US government data (public domain) except the IMF copper price
sources.vintage: vintage - every published vintage since mid-2011; a value is available from the end of its release day

sources.name: EIA-860M Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory
sources.vintage: vintage - one archived file per month since July 2015; available 30 days after the reference month
sources.content: Planned and newly operating generating capacity by technology (gas turbines, batteries, solar, wind, engines and fuel cells)

sources.name: EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor
sources.vintage: lagged - current files only; monthly average demand assumed public 10 days after month end
sources.content: Hourly demand by balancing authority and PJM sub-region (Dominion zone), July 2015 onward

sources.name: EIA-861M monthly retail electricity sales
sources.vintage: lagged - current file only; assumed public 60 days after month end
sources.content: Commercial-sector electricity sales in Virginia and Texas (data center load)

sources.name: US Census Bureau, Value of Construction Put in Place (data center category)
sources.vintage: lagged - current revised history only; assumed public 35 days after month end; revisions are not point-in-time
sources.content: Private construction spending on data centers, monthly since 2014

sources.name: Generator interconnection queues (MISO, CAISO, NYISO)
sources.terms: Public files published by each grid operator
sources.vintage: event - each request keeps its queue-entry date; withdrawn requests stay in the files, so new requests per month are rebuilt without survivorship
sources.content: 8,500 requests with fuel, MW and status

sources.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, TABS project registrations
sources.content: 277 data center construction registrations since December 2018 with estimated cost

sources.name: Tenders Electronic Daily (EU public procurement journal), search API v3
sources.terms: EU open data (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, reuse allowed with attribution)
sources.content: About 9,600 contract award notices for transformers, switchgear and power cable since 2018

sources.name: Indeed Hiring Lab job postings index
sources.terms: CC BY 4.0, attribution Indeed Hiring Lab
sources.vintage: lagged - current file only (Indeed revises the index); assumed public 7 days after month end
sources.content: US job postings by occupational sector, daily since February 2020

sources.name: UN Comtrade (public preview API)
sources.terms: UN Comtrade terms; the anonymous preview API has a request quota
sources.vintage: lagged - current database; assumed public 75 days after month end
sources.content: US monthly imports and exports for six HS codes, January 2015 to November 2023. The anonymous quota (HTTP 403) stopped later US months and all Japan and Korea series; nothing was done to get around it

sources.name: USAspending.gov federal awards
sources.content: Largest federal contract awards per company, shown on the timeline; federal buying is too small a share of these companies' sales to model

sources.name: CRSP daily stock returns (via WRDS, licensed)
sources.terms: Licensed; used locally for the excess-return tests only. No CRSP data is in this repository or on the dashboard
sources.content: Daily total returns of 12 target companies and the S&P 500, through December 2024

sources.name: BLS public API
sources.content: Not used; the same PPI series come from ALFRED, with vintages

sources.name: ERCOT MIS reports (Texas interconnection and large-load reports)
Berkeley Lab 'Queued Up' interconnection dataset
sources.terms: Behind a bot challenge (HTTP 403 to scripts)
sources.content: Not used; the operators' own queue files are used instead

sources.name: PJM and SPP interconnection queues
sources.terms: PJM's export needs a registered API key; SPP's public export lists active requests only (survivorship)

sources.name: Satellite-derived datasets (NASA Black Marble night lights, Sentinel-5P NO2)
sources.terms: Free, but downloads need an Earthdata or Copernicus account
sources.content: Not built; would need an account the project does not have

sources.name: Earnings-call transcripts
sources.terms: Commercial transcript providers do not allow redistribution
sources.content: Not used; company statements come from 8-K press releases and annual reports filed with the SEC instead
